title: GW near-gap replay noise floor is ~1.3e-04 eV on the pinned stack - acceptance tolerances must sit above it
symptom: A byte-identical control replay of the bn-k222 v1 case (same binaries, inputs, resources) reproduced KS bit-for-bit and EXX to 1e-05 eV, but the near-gap GW states shifted by up to 1.3e-04 eV - enough to exceed a 1e-04 eV tolerance and false-fail a perfectly healthy run. Second measurement at the converged 24-point grid: floor 2.4e-03 eV - 18x the 16-point floor. The floor depends on the configuration (more frequency points, more summation terms), so it must be re-measured after any material config change and the tolerance re-calibrated above the CURRENT floor.
root_cause: The GW quasiparticle summation is not bitwise deterministic across runs (parallel reduction ordering in the self-energy chain). KS eigenvalues and the EXX chain are effectively deterministic; only the correlated part carries the noise.
minimal_fix: Calibrate each case's GW tolerance above the CURRENT config's measured replay noise floor (1e-03 eV at 16 points, 1e-02 eV at 24 points), and keep KS/EXX at the tight convention. Any candidate rejection must exceed the floor by orders of magnitude to be meaningful (the nfreq=24 rejection sat at 2300x).
validation: One control replay per stack generation is enough to measure the floor; re-measure whenever the stack or resources change.
avoid: Setting GW tolerances at or below the replay noise floor (guaranteed false failures), or loosening tolerances without a measured floor to justify them.

parameters.tolerance: GW >= 10x measured replay floor; KS/EXX 1e-04 eV
